newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia rebels kidnap entire town council.
newsitem.headline: Colombia rebels kidnap entire town council.

text.p: Leftist rebels kidnapped all members of a town council in northern Colombia as part of their campaign to sabotage forthcoming local elections in October, police sources said on Sunday.

Nine officials, including the town treasurer, from Simiti, in northern Bolivar province were seized as they went to a meeting Saturday on the orders of one of the guerrilla armies that operates in the area.

A police spokesman said it was not immediately clear whether the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC), the country's largest rebel force, or the smaller Cuban-inspired National Liberation Army (ELN) had carried out the kidnapping.

"The ELN came into Simiti and called out all the townspeople and gave them a class on politics...but it seems the councilors may have been kidnapped by the FARC," a police spokesman in the regional capital Cartagena said.

No demands have yet been set for the officials' release, the spokesman said. Simiti has had no police presence since about 100 rebels overran the town on June 30, destroying the barracks and killing three policemen.

Earlier this month the ELN kidnapped five mayors in southern Narino province and killed a senator in northeast Norte de Santander province. The FARC meanwhile has forced all candidates for the Oct. 26 mayoral elections to stand down in a number of towns in southern and eastern Colombia.

Both rebel groups have pledged to disrupt the elections, in which provincial governors will also be elected, and have threatened to kill any candidates of opposing political views who dare to campaign in their zones of influence.
